title: Colony Glacier Crash Recovery B-Roll
description: On November 22nd, 1952, a C-124 crashed into Mount Gannett in the Chugach Mountain Range in Alaska. On June 9th, 2012, the Army National Guard located some wreckage from the C-124 crash on a routine training mission. Every year since, a team has traveled to the glacier to recover human remains and aircraft wreckage.

transcript.text: So a little bit of background on the 22nd of November in 1952.
The C-124 departed from Almondor, from McCord Air Force Base in Route 2, Elmondorff.
There were 52 members on board. You can see the breakdown here.
There were 42 where Air Force. 12 of those were crew members.
8 were from the Army. 1 was from the Navy and 1 was from the Marine Corps.
They lost communication with the plane. It crashed into the side of Mount Gannet, which is over here in reference to J-Barry.
You can see they were fairly close to the base.
So if you want to fast forward now, 60 years, the Alaska Army National Guard, they were doing a routine flying mission.
And they flew over Colony Glacier. They saw some yellow debris on the glacier so they landed.
And they rummaged through it, brought some of that back, and they identified it as the C-124 that had previously crashed.
This is where they landed in this area here, and this is where the crash site was.
So this is approximately 12 miles that this wreckage has traveled down the mountain onto the glacier.
Every year since it was discovered, our team has gone up to the glacier and recovered all of the human remains possible and their personal effects to be reassociated back to those family members.
